definition_zh: 药丸；药片；口服避孕药；不得不咽下的苦事
definition_en: a small round solid piece of medicine swallowed whole, also the daily contraceptive tablet and, figuratively, an unpleasant thing that has to be accepted
core_image: 一粒裹着糖衣的小圆药丸，静静躺在一只摊开的手心里
scene: 深夜的宿舍里，桌上摊着几板感冒药，搪瓷杯里的水还冒着热气。He shook one pill into his palm and swallowed it with a gulp of water.
sceneCN: 这里的 pill 是「药丸、药片」（第 1 个义项：整粒吞服的固体药）；句意是他抖出一粒药丸放在手心，就着一大口水咽下去。图中可辨识物件：药板、搪瓷杯、台灯。

collocations.zh: 把难接受的事说得顺耳些

derivatives.zh: 由 pill 与 box 复合而成，义为「药盒」
由 pill 与 bottle 复合而成，义为「药瓶」

senses.title: A small solid dose of medicine
senses.definition: a small round or oval piece of medicine that is swallowed whole with water
senses.definitionCN: 用水整粒吞下的小圆或椭圆形药物
senses.example: Take one pill with water after breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 早饭后用水送服一粒药。
senses.why: Latin pilula meant a little ball, because early pharmacists rolled each dose by hand into a round pellet, and that shape became the name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pilula 本义是「小球」，因为早期药剂师把每一剂药用手搓成圆粒，这个形状后来就成了名字。

senses.title: The daily contraceptive tablet
senses.definition: the contraceptive pill taken once a day, usually referred to with the definite article
senses.definitionCN: 每天服用一次的避孕药，通常与定冠词连用
senses.example: She has been on the pill since college.
senses.exampleCN: 她从大学起就一直在服用口服避孕药。
senses.why: Because the contraceptive is taken every day and is the pill most often meant in conversation, the fixed phrase the pill narrowed to it alone.
senses.whyCN: 因为避孕药需要每天服用，也是日常对话里最常提到的那种药，固定说法 the pill 便单独指向了它。

senses.title: Something humiliating that must be accepted
senses.titleCN: 苦果；不得不忍受的难堪
senses.definition: an unpleasant fact, defeat or insult that one has no choice but to accept
senses.definitionCN: 不得不接受的不快事实、失败或羞辱
senses.example: Losing the final was a bitter pill for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉决赛对整支队伍来说是一枚难咽的苦果。
senses.why: A pill that tastes bitter still has to be swallowed for the sake of the cure, so the image of forced medicine became a metaphor for forced humiliation.
senses.whyCN: 再苦的药丸也得为了治病咽下去，于是「被迫吃药」的画面就变成了「被迫受辱」的比喻。

intro.en: Pill traces back to a Latin word for a little ball, since early doses were rolled by hand; English most likely took the word from Dutch rather than straight from Latin.
intro.cn: pill 可追到拉丁语中表示「小球」的词，因为早期药丸是手工搓成的；英语多半是从荷兰语而非直接从拉丁语借入。

items.en: Pila named a ball or any round object, and it sits at the base of the whole family.
items.cn: pila 指球或任何圆形物体，是这一族词共同的底座。

items.en: The suffix -ula shrank pila into pilula, a little ball, the word used for a rounded dose of medicine.
items.cn: 后缀 -ula 把 pila 缩小成 pilula，即「小球」，用来指搓圆的药剂。

items.en: Middle Dutch pille named a small round medicine; most dictionaries hold that English borrowed the word from here or from a very close form.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pille 指圆形小药丸；多数词典认为英语是从这里或与之极接近的形式借入的。

items.en: Middle English pille covered any small ball of medicine, whether chewed, swallowed or dissolved in liquid.
items.cn: 中古英语 pille 泛指各种小药丸，无论嚼服、吞服还是化在水里。

items.en: Modern English cut the word down to pill and let it cover the contraceptive and, in a bitter pill, any humiliation that has to be endured.
items.cn: 现代英语把词缩为 pill，并让它兼指避孕药，以及在 a bitter pill 中任何必须忍受的难堪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that merely share letters with pill; the near-meaning group gathers other names for a measured dose of medicine.
note.cn: 形近组收只是与 pill 拼写相近的词；近义组收其他表示一剂药的词。

entries.definition: A heap of things lying one on another; it only looks like pill in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 一堆叠放的东西；只是拼写和 pill 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A cushion for the head; it shares the first letters but comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 睡觉垫头的软垫；只是开头字母相同，来自另一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: To strip off an outer layer, or the skin of a fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 剥去外层，或指果皮。

entries.definition: A small flat round dose of medicine, usually pressed rather than rolled.
entries.definitionCN: 压制成的小圆片药，多由压制而非搓成。

entries.definition: A dose of medicine enclosed in a soluble shell.
entries.definitionCN: 装在可溶外壳里的一剂药。

entries.definition: The measured amount of a medicine taken at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 一次服用的药量。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin ball shrunk by a suffix, and the family keeps that shape: something small, round and easy to swallow.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「球」被后缀缩小的结果，同族词也保留着这个形状：小而圆、容易吞下。

normal.en: Pill starts as Latin pila, a ball, and pilula is simply a little ball; a pill is medicine rolled into that shape.
normal.cn: pill 源自拉丁语 pila（球），pilula 就是「小球」，药丸正是被搓成这个形状的药。

normal.en: The suffix -ula marks something smaller, so pilula is a pila shrunk down, which is exactly what one dose is.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ula 表示更小，pilula 就是缩小版的 pila，正好对应一剂的量。

normal.en: Sleeping pill and pain pill put the purpose in front of the word, the usual English way of building compounds.
normal.cn: sleeping pill 与 pain pill 把用途放在词前，这是英语构成复合词的常见方式。

normal.en: On the pill is a fixed phrase for the contraceptive, and the definite article does the narrowing.
normal.cn: on the pill 是口服避孕药的固定说法，定冠词完成了这层收窄。

normal.en: A bitter pill to swallow keeps the taste of medicine inside a metaphor about humiliation.
normal.cn: a bitter pill to swallow 把药的味道留在了关于难堪的比喻里。

abstract.en: A medicine small enough to swallow whole is a neat picture of anything you must simply get down.
abstract.cn: 一粒小到能整颗吞下的药，正好比喻那些只能硬着头皮接受的事。

abstract.en: One word for a cure and for a humiliation shows how close relief and endurance can sit.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指解药又指难堪，说明缓解与忍耐往往只隔一层。

abstract.en: A daily pill turns a decision into a habit, and language quietly follows the habit.
abstract.cn: 每天一粒药把决定变成习惯，语言也随之悄悄跟上了这个习惯。

examples.en: Take one pill with water after breakfast.
examples.cn: 早饭后用水送服一粒药。

examples.en: She has been on the pill since college.
examples.cn: 她从大学起就一直在服用口服避孕药。

examples.en: Losing the final was a bitter pill for the whole team.
examples.cn: 输掉决赛对整支队伍来说是一枚难咽的苦果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮儿」——小药丸外面总裹着一层糖皮儿，念起来就是 pill。

root: 拉丁语 pila（球）加指小后缀 -ula 得 pilula（小丸），一般认为经中古荷兰语 pille 进入英语，义为「小圆药丸」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a round medicine; from there the word narrows to the contraceptive and widens again into a metaphor for what must be endured.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是圆形的药；由此收窄指避孕药，又向外扩展成「必须忍受之事」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small sugar-coated ball of medicine resting in an open palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒裹着糖衣的小药丸躺在摊开的手心里。

branches.en: a round pellet rolled between thumb and forefinger
branches.cn: 拇指与食指之间搓成的小圆丸

branches.en: a hand tipping one dose into an open palm
branches.cn: 掌心接住一粒倒出来的药

branches.en: a blister pack on a bathroom shelf, one dose taken each night
branches.cn: 浴室架上的药板，每晚取走一粒

branches.en: a cup of water raised to get something bitter down
branches.cn: 端起水杯把苦的东西咽下去

branches.en: a daily habit that is also a decision
branches.cn: 既是每日习惯，也是一个决定

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin noun for a ball, a Latin suffix that makes it small, and the Dutch and English forms that turned a pellet into a tablet.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「球」的拉丁名词、把它变小的拉丁后缀，以及把药丸变成药片的荷兰语与英语形式共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin gave the word its ball-shaped base and the suffix that shrank it, and those two forms are the true relatives of pill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给了这个词「球」的底座和把它缩小的后缀，这两个形式才是 pill 真正的同族词。

definition_zh: 柱子；支柱；栋梁；柱状物；桥墩；门柱
definition_en: a tall upright support of any shape, or a person or thing regarded as essential to a group or system
core_image: 一根方正的立柱顶住门廊，旁边一根圆柱只作装饰；同一词也指撑起整座建筑的那个人
scene: 门廊左侧的方柱已被风雨磨圆了棱角。The central pillar takes most of the roof's weight, while the others only frame the entrance.
sceneCN: 这里 pillar 指「建筑中直立的支撑柱」（第 1 个义项：柱子、支柱）；句意为中央那根柱子承担屋顶的大部分重量，其余只用来框住入口。图中可辨识物件：门廊、方柱、圆柱、屋顶；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 有柱子的
（英）邮筒
柱状的
社会栋梁
支柱产业

senses.title: An upright architectural support
senses.definition: a tall upright support, square or round, often ornamental as well as structural
senses.definitionCN: 高而直立的支撑件，方或圆，常兼具装饰与承重作用
senses.example: A square pillar flanked each side of the porch.
senses.exampleCN: 门廊两侧各立一根方柱。
senses.why: the Latin source meant a pillar of any section, so the word never required the roundness of a classical column.
senses.whyCN: 其拉丁来源指任意截面的柱子，因此这个词从不要求古典柱那样的圆形。

senses.title: A person who holds up a community
senses.definition: a person regarded as a main support of a community or institution
senses.definitionCN: 被视为社区或机构主要支撑的人
senses.example: The old teacher was a pillar of the village for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老教师五十年来一直是村里的栋梁。
senses.why: the metaphor is structural and moral at once: remove the person and the group sags.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻同时是结构与道德的：去掉这个人，群体就会塌下去。

senses.title: An essential part of a system
senses.definition: a component on which a system depends, such as a sector of an economy
senses.definitionCN: 某个系统所依赖的组成部分，如经济中的某个部门
senses.example: Tourism is a pillar of the island's income.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是这座岛屿收入的支柱。
senses.why: systems are described as buildings, so their load-bearing parts are described as pillars.
senses.whyCN: 系统被描述为建筑，因此其承重部分被说成柱子。

senses.title: A tall narrow mass
senses.definition: a tall narrow shape of smoke, light, salt or rock
senses.definitionCN: 烟、光、盐或岩石形成的细高形状
senses.example: A pillar of salt stood where the tide had cut the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水切开的崖边立着一根盐柱。
senses.why: the shape is enough: the word needs no load and no building.
senses.whyCN: 形状就够了：这个词不需要荷载，也不需要建筑。

senses.title: A bridge pier
senses.definition: the vertical support that carries a bridge span
senses.definitionCN: 承托桥梁跨度的竖向支撑
senses.example: The middle pillar of the bridge has been rebuilt twice.
senses.exampleCN: 桥的中墩已重建过两次。
senses.why: engineering uses the plain word for any vertical load path, not only for ornamental shafts.
senses.whyCN: 工程用这个朴素词指任何竖向承重路径，而不只用于装饰柱。

senses.title: A gatepost
senses.definition: a short sturdy post marking or carrying a gate or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 标记或承托门与边界的短粗立柱
senses.example: The gate hangs between two brick pillars.
senses.exampleCN: 大门挂在两根砖柱之间。
senses.why: one of the oldest uses is simply a post that marks a threshold.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法之一就是标记门槛的一根柱子。

senses.title: One of three policy supports
senses.definition: in policy language, one of several coordinated supports of a system, as in pension pillars
senses.definitionCN: 政策语言中某个体系的几根协同支柱之一，如养老金三支柱
senses.example: The report describes the three pillars of the pension scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述该养老金方案的三根支柱。
senses.why: policy analysts borrowed the architectural image to show that the system fails if one support is removed.
senses.whyCN: 政策分析者借用建筑意象，说明抽掉一根支柱体系就会失效。

senses.title: A pillar industry
senses.definition: a sector that carries a large share of a region's output and employment
senses.definitionCN: 承担某地区大部分产出与就业的产业部门
senses.example: Shipbuilding became the pillar of the coastal economy.
senses.exampleCN: 造船业成为沿海经济的支柱。
senses.why: the fixed phrase turns the metaphor into an economic category with measurable weight.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定说法把比喻变成一个有可测分量的经济范畴。

intro.en: Pillar comes from a Latin word for a pillar through Old French, and it has always meant a support of any shape. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pillar 经古法语来自拉丁语中表示「柱子」的词，历来指任意形状的支撑。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pila named a pillar or pier; it is written the same as the word for a ball, and the two are usually treated as separate nouns.
items.cn: pila 指柱子或墩柱；它与表示「球」的词拼写相同，通常被视为两个不同的名词。

items.en: A derived noun pilare named a pillar or a supporting post in later Latin.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中派生名词 pilare 指柱子或支撑柱。

items.en: Old French pilier carried the word into English, where it named a support in a building or a gate.
items.cn: 古法语 pilier 把这个词带入英语，指建筑或大门中的支撑。

items.en: By the medieval period the word covered bridge piers and gateposts as well as interior shafts.
items.cn: 到中世纪，这个词除室内柱身外还涵盖桥墩与门柱。

items.en: From the sixteenth century a trusted person could be called a pillar of the community or of the church.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，受信赖的人可被称为社区或教会的栋梁。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the ancestry of pila before Latin is not established, and whether it is connected to the ball word is disputed; no shared origin has been demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：pila 在拉丁语之前的谱系未得到证明，它与表示「球」的词是否有联系也有争议；尚无证据显示两者同源。

note.en: Group one holds upright-support words that overlap with pillar; group two holds metaphorical supports and tall masses.
note.cn: 第一组是与 pillar 重叠的直立支撑词；第二组是比喻性支撑与高柱体。

entries.definition: A support, usually round and governed by an order; a pillar may be square and need follow no order.
entries.definitionCN: 通常为圆形且受柱式规范的支撑；pillar 可为方形、无须遵循柱式。

entries.definition: A thick masonry support between openings or under a bridge; it is heavier and more wall-like than a pillar.
entries.definitionCN: 开口之间或桥下的厚砌体支撑；比 pillar 更厚重、更像墙。

entries.definition: A plain upright piece of timber or metal; pillar sounds more monumental and more permanent.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素木制或金属直立件；pillar 听起来更宏大、更持久。

entries.definition: A small pillar; the suffix makes it a minor architectural member.
entries.definitionCN: 小柱子；后缀使它成为次要建筑构件。

entries.definition: The chief support of a system, from a sailing term for the rope holding a mast; it is closer to pillar sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 体系的主要支撑，来自固定桅杆的航海术语；更接近 pillar 的第二个义项。

entries.definition: A support placed under something to hold it up; it is usually temporary and rarely ornamental.
entries.definitionCN: 置于某物下方以托住的支撑，通常临时且少装饰。

entries.definition: Anything that holds weight or sustains a system; it is the neutral term that pillar makes concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 任何承重或维持体系之物；是中性的总称，pillar 使之具体化。

entries.definition: The central strength of a group or system, from the spine; it stresses unity rather than vertical support.
entries.definitionCN: 群体或体系的核心力量，来自脊柱；强调统一性而非竖向支撑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin source, the real bridge and gate uses, and the real policy phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁来源、真实的桥梁与门柱用法、真实的政策说法。

normal.en: The word never required a round shaft, so a square gatepost is as much a pillar as a marble column.
normal.cn: 这个词从不要求圆形柱身，因此方形门柱与大理石圆柱一样是 pillar。

normal.en: The family runs pillar, pillared, pillaret, pillar-box, pillar-like.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pillar、pillared、pillaret、pillar-box、pillar-like。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: stone pillar, pillar of society, bridge pillar, pillar industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：石柱、社会栋梁、桥墩、支柱产业。

normal.en: The metaphor is load-bearing: take the person away and the group sags.
normal.cn: 这个比喻是承重的：把人抽走，群体就会塌。

normal.en: A pillar of salt and a pillar of smoke need no building at all.
normal.cn: 盐柱与烟柱根本不需要建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a village where one person is literally holding up the roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄里真有一个人托着屋顶。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge standing on one leg in the middle of a river.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥用一条腿立在河心。

abstract.en: Picture a policy report drawn as a temple with three columns.
abstract.cn: 想象一份政策报告被画成一座有三根柱子的神庙。

examples.en: The pillar at the gate carries the date of the first owner.
examples.cn: 门柱上刻着第一任主人的日期。

examples.en: She was a pillar of the hospital's volunteer service.
examples.cn: 她是这家医院志愿服务的栋梁。

examples.en: A pillar of cloud rose over the burning refinery.
examples.cn: 燃烧的炼油厂上方升起一根烟柱。

dict_mnemonic.text: pila（柱子）+ 英语名词尾 → 直立的支撑 → 柱子、支柱、栋梁

root: 古法语 pilier 来自中世纪拉丁 pilare，其源头是拉丁 pila「柱子、墩柱」；英语 pillar。pila 的更早谱系不确定，与表示「球」的 pila 是否有关尚无证据。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one upright piece: a building support becomes a person, a system part, a tall mass, a bridge pier, a gatepost, a policy support and an industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一根直立件展开：建筑支撑成为人、体系部件、高柱体、桥墩、门柱、政策支柱与产业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain upright block that holds something heavier than itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块朴素的直立体，托着比它更重的东西。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL SUPPORT: a shaft, a pier and a gatepost are the same block in three positions.
branches.cn: 实体支撑：柱身、桥墩与门柱，是同一块直立体在三个位置。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a trusted member is described as holding the group up.
branches.cn: 人：受信赖的成员被描述为托住群体的人。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: economic sectors and policy supports are load-bearing parts.
branches.cn: 体系：经济部门与政策支撑都是承重部件。

branches.en: THE MASS: smoke, salt and light keep only the tall narrow shape.
branches.cn: 体量：烟、盐与光只保留了细高的形状。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: the metaphor hardens into the fixed term pillar industry.
branches.cn: 范畴：比喻固化为「支柱产业」这一固定术语。

intro.en: Pillar is a borrowed noun with almost no productive affix of its own; its family is built with English endings and fixed compounds.
intro.cn: pillar 是借入名词，本身几乎没有能产词缀；其词族由英语词尾与固定复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pila and the later pilare are the direct sources; English formed pillared and pillaret from the noun, not from new Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pila 与后期的 pilare 是直接来源；英语的 pillared 与 pillaret 是从名词构成，而非新的拉丁词。

items.example: Pilare named the pier of a bridge.
A stone pilier framed the gate.
A pillared porch marks the entrance.
items.exampleCN: 一道有柱的门廊标出入口。

items.example: The red pillar-box stands at the corner.

items.meaning: a sector that carries an economy
items.example: Steel was once a pillar industry here.
items.exampleCN: 钢铁一度是这里的支柱产业。

definition_zh: 枕头；抱枕；靠垫；枕状垫块
definition_en: a soft cushion that supports the head in bed, and by extension any cushion one leans on or a pad placed under part of the body
core_image: 一只被压出浅浅头形的白枕头，枕套边上还留着折痕
scene: 雨夜的卧铺车厢里，窗帘半掩，铺位上摊着一条薄被。She punched the pillow twice and turned to face the window.
sceneCN: 这里的 pillow 是「枕头」（第 1 个义项：睡觉时垫头的软垫）；句意是她把枕头拍了两下，转身面向车窗。图中可辨识物件：窗帘、薄被、铺位。

collocations.phrase: rest one's head on a pillow

derivatives.zh: 由 pillow 与 case 复合而成，义为「枕套」
由 pillow 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「枕状的；柔软的」

senses.title: A cushion for the head in bed
senses.definition: a soft bag filled with feathers, foam or grain, placed under the head while sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 装满羽毛、海绵或谷物的软袋，睡觉时垫在头下
senses.example: He fell asleep as soon as his head touched the pillow.
senses.exampleCN: 他的头一碰到枕头就睡着了。
senses.why: Old English pyle borrowed the Latin word for a cushion, and the first job of that cushion was to hold up a sleeping head.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pyle 借自拉丁语中表示「垫子」的词，而这种垫子最初的任务就是在睡梦中托住脑袋。

senses.title: A decorative cushion for leaning on
senses.definition: a smaller cushion kept on a sofa or chair so that sitting becomes more comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 放在沙发或椅子上、让坐姿更舒服的小垫子
senses.example: Three striped pillows were stacked at one end of the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 沙发一端叠着三个条纹靠垫。
senses.why: Once cushions moved from the bed to the living room, the old word travelled with them and now covers anything soft you lean against.
senses.whyCN: 垫子从床上搬到客厅之后，旧词也跟着搬了过去，如今泛指任何可以靠着的柔软之物。

senses.title: A pad that supports part of the body
senses.definition: a pad or block placed under a limb or a machine part to support it
senses.definitionCN: 垫在肢体或机器部件下方起承托作用的垫块
senses.example: The nurse slid a foam pillow under his injured ankle.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把一块泡沫垫塞到他受伤的脚踝下面。
senses.why: A pillow does one thing well, holding something up softly, so nursing and engineering borrowed the name for any pad that supports.
senses.whyCN: 枕头只把一件事做好，就是柔软地托住东西，于是护理和工程都借这个词来指任何起承托作用的垫子。

intro.en: Pillow is an Old English word for a cushion, and the cushion itself came from Latin; the exact route through the Germanic languages is not fully certain.
intro.cn: pillow 是古英语中表示垫子的词，而垫子这个概念来自拉丁语；它经由日耳曼诸语的具体路径并不完全确定。

items.en: Pulvinus named a cushion or bolster, and it could also mean the cushioned couch on which images of the gods were placed.
items.cn: pulvinus 指垫子、长靠枕，也可指安放神像的软榻。

items.en: Germanic speakers took the Latin cushion word over; the reconstructed form is usually written with an asterisk, and the exact route is described as uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语借用了拉丁语的「垫子」一词；重构形式通常带星号，具体路径一般认为并不确定。

items.en: Old English pyle meant both pillow and cushion, so the bed sense and the general sense started together.
items.cn: 古英语 pyle 同时指枕头和垫子，床上义与泛指义从一开始就并存。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word pilwe, with a w that later hardened into the modern ending.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 pilwe，词尾的 w 后来固定成现代形式。

items.en: Modern English settled on pillow and built compounds such as pillowcase and pillow talk on top of it.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 pillow，并在其上构成 pillowcase、pillow talk 等复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that only share letters or a syllable with pillow; the near-meaning group collects other soft supports.
note.cn: 形近组收只是与 pillow 共享字母或音节的词；近义组收其他柔软的承托物。

entries.definition: A small round dose of medicine; it only echoes the start of pillow, and the two have different Latin sources.
entries.definitionCN: 小圆药丸；只是与 pillow 开头相近，两者的拉丁来源不同。

entries.definition: A tree with long bending branches, often planted beside water.
entries.definitionCN: 枝条细长下垂、常种在水边的树。

entries.definition: To swell out like a sail filled with wind.
entries.definitionCN: 像灌满风的帆那样鼓起。

entries.definition: A tall upright post that holds up a building.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑建筑的高立柱。

entries.definition: A soft pad used to sit on or lean against.
entries.definitionCN: 用来坐或靠的软垫。

entries.definition: A long firm pillow, or to strengthen something.
entries.definitionCN: 长而结实的枕头；也指加强。

entries.definition: The part of a seat that supports the head.
entries.definitionCN: 座椅上支撑头部的部分。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the name of a cushion and never lost that softness; every later sense is a cushion doing its old job somewhere new.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「垫子」的名字开始，始终没丢掉那份柔软；后来每个义项都是垫子在新的地方做着旧工作。

normal.en: Pillow and Latin pulvinus both name a cushion, so softness is built into the word from the first record.
normal.cn: pillow 与拉丁语 pulvinus 都指垫子，柔软从最早的记录起就写进了这个词。

normal.en: Old English pyle already meant both pillow and cushion, which is why the bed sense and the sofa sense never fully split.
normal.cn: 古英语 pyle 本就兼指枕头和垫子，所以床上义与沙发义始终没有彻底分开。

normal.en: Pillowcase joins pillow to case, the ordinary English way of naming a cover for a thing.
normal.cn: pillowcase 把 pillow 与 case 组合起来，正是英语给某物的外套命名的常见办法。

normal.en: Pillow talk keeps the word in bed and turns it into a name for what is said there.
normal.cn: pillow talk 把词留在床上，用来指那里说出的私房话。

normal.en: Pillowy adds -y to say soft like a pillow, a suffix that turns a noun into a quality.
normal.cn: pillowy 加 -y 表示「像枕头一样软」，这个后缀把名词变成了性质。

abstract.en: A pillow is the one object whose whole purpose is to be forgotten while you sleep.
abstract.cn: 枕头是唯一一种整个用途就是让人睡着后忘掉它的东西。

abstract.en: Softness that holds you up is a useful picture for any support you stop noticing.
abstract.cn: 柔软的承托，是形容那些你不再察觉的支撑的好画面。

abstract.en: The word moved from bed to sofa to hospital without changing shape, only the place of rest.
abstract.cn: 这个词从床到沙发再到病房，形状没变，变的只是歇息的地方。

examples.en: He fell asleep as soon as his head touched the pillow.
examples.cn: 他的头一碰到枕头就睡着了。

examples.en: She bought two new pillow cases for the spare room.
examples.cn: 她给客房买了两只新枕套。

examples.en: The nurse slid a foam pillow under his injured ankle.
examples.cn: 护士把一块泡沫垫塞到他受伤的脚踝下面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮篓」——脑袋像装进一只软皮篓子，那就是枕头。

root: 古英语 pyle 经西日耳曼语借自拉丁语 pulvinus（垫子、靠枕），最初指睡觉时垫在头下的软垫。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the cushion under a sleeping head; the other senses carry the same soft support to the sofa and to the sickbed.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是睡梦中垫在头下的软垫；其余义项把同样的柔软承托带到沙发与病床。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white pillow with a shallow dent where a head has rested.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只白枕头被压出浅浅的头形凹痕。

branches.en: a head sinking into a soft bag at night
branches.cn: 夜里脑袋陷进软软的一袋填充物

branches.en: a hand fluffing the pillow before sleep
branches.cn: 睡前用手把枕头拍松

branches.en: three cushions stacked at one end of a sofa
branches.cn: 沙发一端叠着三个靠垫

branches.en: a foam pad slipped under an injured ankle
branches.cn: 垫在受伤脚踝下的泡沫垫

branches.en: soft support wherever the body rests
branches.cn: 身体歇着的地方都有柔软的承托

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin cushion noun, its Germanic and Old English descendants, and two English compounds that keep the softness in view.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语的「垫子」名词、它在日耳曼语和古英语中的后裔，以及两个保留柔软意象的英语复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin pulvinus is the cushion behind the English word, and its longer relative pulvinar names the cushioned couch of the gods.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pulvinus 是英语这个词背后的「垫子」，它更长的一个同族词 pulvinar 指安放神像的软榻。

items.meaning: cushioned couch for images of the gods

definition_zh: 飞行员；引水员；驾驶；引导；试验性的
definition_en: a person who flies an aircraft or guides a ship into harbour, the act of steering or guiding something, and a small trial version launched before the full thing
core_image: 驾驶舱里一只手握住操纵杆，前方跑道在雨雾里亮起一排灯
scene: 清晨的机场笼着薄雾，登机梯旁站着一个穿深色制服的人。The pilot walked slowly around the wing and checked it before boarding.
sceneCN: 这里的 pilot 是「飞行员」（第 1 个义项：驾驶飞机的人）；句意是飞行员绕着机翼慢慢走了一圈，登机前做了检查。图中可辨识物件：登机梯、机翼、跑道灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 pilot 加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「引航；引航费」
由 pilot 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无人驾驶的」
由 pilot 与 house 复合而成，义为「驾驶室」

senses.title: A person who flies an aircraft
senses.definition: a person trained and licensed to fly an aeroplane or other aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练并取得执照、驾驶飞机的人
senses.example: The pilot warned the passengers about the turbulence ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员提醒乘客前方有气流颠簸。
senses.why: The word first named the person who steers a ship; when machines took to the air, the same steering role handed the title to the flyer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指掌舵行船的人；当机器飞上天空，同一个「掌舵」的角色把称号交给了驾驶飞机的人。

senses.title: A specialist who guides a ship in harbour
senses.definition: a local expert who comes aboard to steer a ship through a harbour or a difficult channel
senses.definitionCN: 登船引导船只通过港口或复杂航道的当地专家
senses.example: A local pilot came aboard to take the ship through the narrow channel.
senses.exampleCN: 一名当地引水员登船，带这艘船穿过狭窄航道。
senses.why: In a harbour the captain hands over control to someone who knows every sandbank, so the oldest sense of a hired guide at the helm survives intact.
senses.whyCN: 在港口，船长会把控制权交给熟悉每一处沙洲的人，于是「受雇掌舵的向导」这个最古老的义项完整地留了下来。

senses.title: To steer or guide something
senses.definition: to steer an aircraft, boat or vehicle, or to guide a process through its early stages
senses.definitionCN: 操纵飞机、船只或车辆，或引导某个过程走过最初阶段
senses.example: She piloted the boat through the gap in the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 她驾着小船穿过礁石间的缺口。
senses.why: English turns a role into a verb very readily, so whoever is the pilot simply does the piloting.
senses.whyCN: 英语很习惯把角色直接变成动词，所以当 pilot 的人做的事就叫 pilot。

senses.title: Done as a trial before a full launch
senses.definition: made or done on a small scale first, in order to test whether a full version will work
senses.definitionCN: 先小规模做出或进行，用来检验完整版本是否可行
senses.example: The company ran a pilot scheme in three cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在三座城市试行了一个方案。
senses.why: A pilot boat goes out ahead of the fleet to test the water, so the first small version of a project borrowed the same name.
senses.whyCN: 引水船会先于船队出海探路，于是项目最初的小规模版本也借用了这个名字。

intro.en: Pilot came into English from the sea, through French and Italian, and its medieval Latin form is the first clearly recorded one; the step before that is disputed.
intro.cn: pilot 从海上经法语和意大利语进入英语，中世纪拉丁语形式是最早清楚可考的形态；再往前的一步则有争议。

items.en: One old suggestion traces the word to Greek pedon, an oar; the link is attractive but has never been proved, so it is best marked as uncertain.
items.cn: 一种旧说法把这个词追到希腊语 pedon（桨）；这条线索很吸引人，但从未得到证实，最好标为不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin pilotus named the man who steers a ship, and it is the earliest form that can be quoted with confidence.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 pilotus 指掌舵行船的人，是能够有把握引用的最早形态。

items.en: Italian pilota carried the nautical sense across Mediterranean trade routes.
items.cn: 意大利语 pilota 沿地中海贸易路线传播了这个航海义。

items.en: Middle French pilot brought the word into English in the fifteenth century, still tied to ships and harbours.
items.cn: 中古法语 pilot 在十五世纪把这个词带进英语，当时仍与船和港口绑定。

items.en: Modern English moved the word from harbour to airfield, then to any small trial that goes first.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从港口搬到了机场，再延伸到任何先走一步的小规模试验。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely resemble pilot in spelling; the near-meaning group collects other people who steer or find the way.
note.cn: 形近组收只是拼写与 pilot 相似的词；近义组收其他掌舵或寻路的人。

entries.definition: The central point on which something turns; the spelling is close but the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 物体转动的中心点；拼写接近，来源不同。

entries.definition: A tall tower that carries cables or marks a route.
entries.definitionCN: 架线或标示路线的高塔。

entries.definition: A person who travels a long way to a holy place.
entries.definitionCN: 长途前往圣地的人。

entries.definition: A person who flies aircraft, an older and more formal word.
entries.definitionCN: 驾驶飞机的人，较旧、较正式的说法。

entries.definition: The crew member who works out the route.
entries.definitionCN: 负责计算航线的机组人员。

entries.definition: The person who steers a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 掌舵行船的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a steering role that has changed element twice, from water to air to the early stage of a project.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个掌舵的角色，换过两次场域：从水上到空中，再到项目的最初阶段。

normal.en: Pilot began at sea: it named the man who steered a ship long before anyone flew.
normal.cn: pilot 起于海上：早在有人飞行之前，它就指掌舵行船的人。

normal.en: Pilotage adds -age to name the work and the fee, the same suffix as in postage.
normal.cn: pilotage 加 -age 表示这份工作和费用，和 postage 用的是同一个后缀。

normal.en: Pilotless adds -less, so a pilotless aircraft is one without the person the word first named.
normal.cn: pilotless 加 -less，所以无人驾驶的飞机就是少了这个词最初指的那个人。

normal.en: Pilot project puts the noun in front as a modifier, and that modifier says the project goes first.
normal.cn: pilot project 把名词放在前面作修饰，这个修饰语说明项目要先走一步。

normal.en: Harbour pilot and airline pilot show the same role in two elements, water and air.
normal.cn: harbour pilot 与 airline pilot 展示了同一个角色在水与空两个场域里的样子。

abstract.en: To pilot something new is to go ahead of everyone else and find the rocks first.
abstract.cn: 试行一件新事，就是走在所有人前面，先摸到暗礁。

abstract.en: The same word covers a ship, a plane and a trial, because all three need someone at the front.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指船、飞机和试验，因为三者都需要有人在最前面。

abstract.en: A pilot project is small on purpose, a way of testing the water before the whole fleet sails.
abstract.cn: 试点项目故意做得小，是在整支船队出发前先试试水深。

examples.en: The pilot warned the passengers about the turbulence ahead.
examples.cn: 飞行员提醒乘客前方有气流颠簸。

examples.en: She piloted the boat through the gap in the reef.
examples.cn: 她驾着小船穿过礁石间的缺口。

examples.en: The company ran a pilot scheme in three cities.
examples.cn: 这家公司在三座城市试行了一个方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派了他」——机长派了他去驾驶飞机，他就是 pilot。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 pilotus（掌舵者）经意大利语 pilota、中古法语 pilot 进入英语；更早的来源一般认为与希腊语 pedon（桨）有关，但不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person who steers; the senses then move from harbour to aircraft, from the role to the action, and finally to anything that goes first as a trial.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是掌舵的人；义项由此从港口转到飞机，从角色转到动作，最后转到任何先行试探的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on the control column while runway lights slide past in the rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握住操纵杆，跑道灯在雨中向后退去。

branches.en: a small boat coming out to meet a ship at the harbour mouth
branches.cn: 港口外一条小船驶向大船

branches.en: a hand on the yoke while the runway lights slide past
branches.cn: 手握操纵杆，跑道灯向后退去

branches.en: a crew walking round the wing in the cold morning air
branches.cn: 机组在清冷的晨风里绕机翼检查

branches.en: a project tested in three towns before a national launch
branches.cn: 项目先在三座城市试运行

branches.en: a single episode filmed to see whether a series will work
branches.cn: 先拍一集，看整部剧能否成立

intro.en: The word is carried by a disputed Greek oar, a medieval Latin helmsman, its Italian and French forms, and two English suffixes that name the trade and its absence.
intro.cn: 这个词由有争议的希腊语「桨」、中世纪拉丁语的掌舵者、它的意大利语与法语形式，以及两个表示行业与「无人」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Only the medieval Latin form is safely attested; the older Greek oar is offered as a possibility rather than a settled fact.
latinIntro.cn: 只有中世纪拉丁语形式有可靠记载；更早的希腊语「桨」只是作为一种可能提出，并非定论。

items.meaning: the work of guiding ships, and the fee for it

definition_zh: 别针；大头针；饰针；插脚；钉住；按住
definition_en: a short thin piece of metal with a sharp point used to fasten things, a decorative brooch, a metal leg on a plug, and the act of holding something firmly in place
core_image: 一枚银亮的别针穿过布料，针尖从另一面探出来
scene: 裁缝铺的午后，长桌上铺满布料，粉笔画的线还很清楚。She fixed the paper pattern to the cloth with a pin before cutting.
sceneCN: 这里的 pin 是「别针、大头针」（第 1 个义项：固定布料的细针）；句意是她用一枚别针把纸样固定在布上，然后才下剪。图中可辨识物件：布料、粉笔线、剪刀。

derivatives.zh: 由 pin 与 hole 复合而成，义为「针孔」
由 pin 与 point 复合而成，义为「精确定位」
由 pin 与 head 复合而成，义为「针头；傻瓜」
由 pin 与 prick 复合而成，义为「针刺般的小孔；刺痛」

senses.title: A short pointed fastener
senses.definition: a short thin piece of metal with a sharp point and a head, used to fasten cloth or paper
senses.definitionCN: 一端尖锐、一端有头的小金属件，用来固定布料或纸张
senses.example: A pin held the two sheets of paper together.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚别针把两张纸固定在一起。
senses.why: Old English pinn named a peg or bolt, and the small pointed fastener kept both the shape and the name.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pinn 指木钉或销子，这种带尖的小固定件既保留了它的形状，也继承了它的名字。

senses.title: A decorative brooch
senses.definition: a small ornamental pin worn on clothing for decoration
senses.definitionCN: 别在衣物上作装饰的小饰针
senses.example: She fastened a gold pin to her collar.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一枚金饰针别在衣领上。
senses.why: Once a pin could hold cloth, it could also hold an ornament, and the jewel fixed on the pin took over the word.
senses.whyCN: 既然别针能固定布料，也就能固定饰物，于是别在针上的珠宝接管了这个词。

senses.title: To fasten or hold firmly
senses.definition: to fasten something with a pin, or to press and hold it so that it cannot move
senses.definitionCN: 用别针固定某物，或压住使其不能移动
senses.example: Pin the hem before you sew it.
senses.exampleCN: 缝之前先把折边别住。
senses.why: The tool became an action in the usual English way: to pin is simply to do what a pin does, hold two things together.
senses.whyCN: 这个工具按英语的惯常方式变成了动作：to pin 就是做别针做的事，把两样东西固定在一起。

senses.title: A metal leg on a plug or chip
senses.definition: one of the metal legs on an electrical plug or component that makes contact with a socket
senses.definitionCN: 插头或电子元件上用来与插座接触的金属脚
senses.example: One pin on the plug was bent, so it would not fit.
senses.exampleCN: 插头上的一个插脚弯了，所以插不进去。
senses.why: Electronics needed a name for the small metal legs pushed into a socket, and their shape and job matched the old fastener exactly.
senses.whyCN: 电子行业需要给插进插座的细小金属脚命名，而它们的形状和用处与旧日的别针完全吻合。

intro.en: Pin is an Old English word for a peg, and the peg itself is usually traced to a Latin word for a point or feather.
intro.cn: pin 是古英语中表示钉子的词，而这种钉子一般认为源自拉丁语中表示「尖端、羽毛」的词。

items.en: Pinna meant a feather, a wing or a point, and it also named the pointed crest of a wall.
items.cn: pinna 指羽毛、翅膀或尖端，也指墙头突出的尖顶。

items.en: Germanic speakers borrowed the Latin point word and used it for a peg; the reconstructed form is usually written with an asterisk, as the borrowing route is not certain.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语借用了拉丁语中表示「尖端」的词来指木钉；重构形式通常带星号，因为借入路径并不确定。

items.en: Old English pinn covered a peg, a bolt and a small pointed fastener.
items.cn: 古英语 pinn 兼指木钉、销子和小型尖头固定件。

items.en: Middle English pin narrowed towards the small pointed fastener used on cloth.
items.cn: 中古英语 pin 收窄到用来固定布料的小尖针。

items.en: Modern English extended the word to jewellery, to the legs of electrical plugs, and to phrases such as pin down.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到首饰、插头插脚，以及 pin down 一类的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely share letters with pin; the near-meaning group collects other small things that hold material together.
note.cn: 形近组收只是与 pin 拼写相近的词；近义组收其他把材料固定在一起的小物件。

entries.definition: An evergreen tree, or to long for something.
entries.definitionCN: 常绿树；也指渴望。

entries.definition: To turn round quickly, or to draw out thread.
entries.definitionCN: 快速旋转；也指纺线。

entries.definition: A tool for writing with ink.
entries.definitionCN: 用墨水写字的工具。

entries.definition: A short nail with a wide flat head.
entries.definitionCN: 短而钉帽宽平的钉子。

entries.definition: A thin pointed tool used for sewing.
entries.definitionCN: 缝纫用的细尖工具。

entries.definition: A small object that holds papers together.
entries.definitionCN: 夹住纸张的小物件。

normalIntro.en: The word is a point that holds things, and every sense keeps something small, sharp or metal at its centre.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个能固定东西的尖端，每个义项的核心都离不了小而尖或小而硬的金属。

normal.en: Pin comes from a Latin word for a point, and every sense still turns on something small and sharp.
normal.cn: pin 来自拉丁语中表示「尖端」的词，每个义项都围绕某个小而尖的东西。

normal.en: Pinhole, pinpoint and pinprick are all built on the same tiny measure, the size of a pin.
normal.cn: pinhole、pinpoint 与 pinprick 都建立在同一个微小的尺度上：一枚别针的大小。

normal.en: Pinhead first meant the head of a pin, and only later became an insult about a small brain.
normal.cn: pinhead 最早指别针的针头，后来才变成说人脑子小的贬称。

normal.en: To pin down is to fix something the way a pin fixes cloth, so a physical act becomes an abstract one.
normal.cn: to pin down 是像别针固定布料那样把事情定住，身体动作由此变成抽象动作。

normal.en: Safety pin and drawing pin put the purpose first, the usual English pattern for compounds.
normal.cn: safety pin 与 drawing pin 把用途放在前面，这是英语复合词的常见模式。

abstract.en: A pin holds things together by being almost nothing, a single point of contact.
abstract.cn: 别针几乎什么都不是，只靠一个接触点就把东西固定住。

abstract.en: Pin down, pin on, pin hopes on: the small metal object becomes a way of fixing blame, facts and hope.
abstract.cn: pin down、pin on、pin hopes on：这枚小金属件变成了固定责任、事实和希望的动词。

abstract.en: What is pinned can also be unpinned, which is why the word carries a hint of something temporary.
abstract.cn: 别住的东西也可以取下来，所以这个词总带着一点临时的意味。

examples.en: A pin held the two sheets of paper together.
examples.cn: 一枚别针把两张纸固定在一起。

examples.en: Pin the hem before you sew it.
examples.cn: 缝之前先把折边别住。

examples.en: One pin on the plug was bent, so it would not fit.
examples.cn: 插头上的一个插脚弯了，所以插不进去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拼」——用别针把两块布拼在一起，这个动作就叫 pin。

root: 古英语 pinn（钉、销）一般认为借自拉丁语 pinna（羽毛、尖端），由「尖」的意象引申为细小的金属别针。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a small pointed metal object; the senses branch into ornament, into the act of fixing, and into the metal legs of modern plugs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是带尖的小金属件；义项分向装饰、固定的动作，以及现代插头上的金属脚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright pin passing through cloth, its point showing on the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚银亮的别针穿过布料，针尖从另一面透出来。

branches.en: two sheets of paper held together by one thin point
branches.cn: 两张纸被一个细尖固定在一起

branches.en: a small gold ornament on a coat collar
branches.cn: 大衣领子上的一枚小金饰

branches.en: a hem held flat under the machine needle
branches.cn: 折边被压平送进缝纫机针下

branches.en: the same small object doing its same small job
branches.cn: 同一个小物件重复着同一件小事

branches.en: a bent metal leg that will not enter the socket
branches.cn: 弯曲的金属插脚插不进插座

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin point, an Old English peg, and four English compounds that all measure something by the size of a pin.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语的「尖端」、古英语的「木钉」，以及四个以别针大小来衡量的英语复合词之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin pinna supplies the point at the root of the word, and the reconstructed Germanic peg is the form that carried it into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pinna 提供了这个词根部的「尖端」，重构的日耳曼语「木钉」则是把它带进英语的形式。

items.meaning: tiny hole made by a pin
the head of a pin; a foolish person
a tiny hole or a sharp little pain

definition_zh: 捏；掐；夹痛；一撮；匮乏
definition_en: to squeeze skin or a small object tightly between the thumb and a finger, the tiny amount held that way, or a painful shortage of money or time
core_image: 拇指与食指合拢，夹住手臂上一小片皮肤，皮肤被提起一道浅浅的褶
scene: 厨房里盐罐快见底了，母亲用两根手指从罐底夹起最后一点白色颗粒，抖进正在冒泡的汤里。She added a pinch of salt to the soup and tasted it again.
sceneCN: 这里 pinch 指「一撮」（第 2 个义项：两指夹住的一点点分量）；句意为她往汤里加了一撮盐，又尝了一次。图中可辨识物件：快空的盐罐、两指间的盐粒、冒泡的汤锅。

derivatives.zh: 由同族的古法语动词 pincier 加表工具的后缀 -ers 构成，义为「钳子；镊子」
由 pinch 加 -ed 构成，义为「消瘦憔悴的；拮据的」
由 pinch 加 -ing 构成，义为「夹脚的；令人难受的」

senses.title: To squeeze something between finger and thumb
senses.definition: to press a person's skin or a small object tightly between the thumb and another finger
senses.definitionCN: 用拇指与另一根手指把皮肤或小物件紧紧夹住
senses.example: She pinched the bridge of her nose and sighed.
senses.exampleCN: 她捏着鼻梁叹了口气。
senses.why: The word began as a name for a small, sharp bite or nip, so the first sense is a quick two-finger grip rather than a full-handed hold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指轻而尖的一下咬或掐，所以第一个义项是两根手指的短促夹合，而不是整只手握住。

senses.title: A very small amount held between the fingers
senses.definition: a quantity of something, especially a powder, that can be held between the thumb and forefinger
senses.definitionCN: 能用拇指与食指夹住的少量东西，尤指粉末
senses.example: Add a pinch of pepper to the sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 往酱汁里加一撮胡椒。
senses.why: Once the gesture has a name, the amount that the gesture carries is named by the same word, which is why cooks measure salt in pinches rather than in grams.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作一旦有了名字，动作所携带的分量也就用同一个词来称呼，所以厨师用「一撮」而不是用克来量盐。

senses.title: A painful shortage of money or time
senses.definition: a period when money, time, or supplies are so short that people feel pressure
senses.definitionCN: 钱、时间或物资短缺到让人感到压力的时期
senses.example: Like most students, he felt the pinch in the last week of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 和大多数学生一样，他在月底最后一周感到了手头拮据。
senses.why: A pinch is a tight squeeze on the skin; moved onto a household budget, the same squeeze becomes the pressure of having too little, so a physical grip turns into an economic one.
senses.whyCN: pinch 是皮肤上被紧紧夹住的一下；把它挪到家庭预算上，同样的夹紧就变成「东西太少」的压力，身体的紧箍于是成了经济的紧箍。

intro.en: Pinch reached English from an Old French verb for nipping and nibbling, and behind that verb most dictionaries assume a Vulgar Latin form built on the Latin word for a point.
intro.cn: pinch 来自古法语中表示掐、小口啃的动词，而多数词典认为那个动词背后是一个以拉丁语「点、刺」为基础构建的俗拉丁语形式。

items.en: Old French pincier meant to pinch, bite, or nibble, and Middle English borrowed it as pinchen in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 pincier 意为捏、咬、小口啃，中古英语在十四世纪把它借入，写作 pinchen。

items.en: Most dictionaries trace the French verb to a reconstructed Vulgar Latin pinctiare, but that form is not recorded anywhere, so this step is only a generally accepted guess.
items.cn: 多数词典把法语动词追溯到重构的俗拉丁语 pinctiare，但这个形式没有任何文献记录，所以这一步只是被普遍接受的推测。

items.en: Latin punctum meant a point or a prick, and the brief, sharp contact of two fingertips fits that image closely.
items.cn: 拉丁语 punctum 意为「点、刺」，两指尖短促而尖的一下接触，与这个意象相当吻合。

items.en: Middle English pinche(n) kept the bodily action and also began to name the small quantity held in the fingers.
items.cn: 中古英语 pinche(n) 保留了身体动作义，同时开始指用手指夹住的那一点点分量。

items.en: Modern English stretches the squeeze onto money and time, so a family can feel the pinch without anyone touching them.
items.cn: 现代英语把这股挤压延伸到金钱与时间上，于是一家人不必真被谁捏一下，也能「感到拮据」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same nipping image or on the same spelling; the near-meaning group gathers other words for gripping, biting and shortage.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个「夹、刺」意象上的词以及拼写相近的词；近义组收其他表示夹、咬与短缺的词。

entries.definition: To hit hard with a fist; it is often traced to the same Latin idea of a sharp point.
entries.definitionCN: 用拳头重击；它也常被追溯到同一个表示「尖点」的拉丁观念。

entries.definition: A tool with two hinged arms for gripping and pulling.
entries.definitionCN: 两臂铰接、用来夹住并拔出的工具；钳子。

entries.definition: Thin and pale, as if the face had been squeezed.
entries.definitionCN: 消瘦苍白的，仿佛脸被捏过一样。

entries.definition: A small cushion for holding pins; it is built on pin rather than on this word, so the resemblance is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 插针用的小垫子；它由 pin 构成而非 pinch，所以只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To press something firmly from two sides.
entries.definitionCN: 从两侧用力压住某物。

entries.definition: To give a small, sharp bite or squeeze.
entries.definitionCN: 轻而尖地咬一下或掐一下。

entries.definition: To hold something tightly and firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 紧紧握住某物。

entries.definition: A situation in which there is not enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物不够用的情况；短缺。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from an Old French verb for nipping, and its family keeps returning to small, sharp contact and to the pressure of having too little.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自古法语中表示掐、咬的动词，它的词族反复回到「短促而尖的接触」以及「东西太少的压力」。

normal.en: Old French pincier meant to nibble as well as to pinch, so the word has always carried a hint of teeth as well as fingers.
normal.cn: 古法语 pincier 既指掐也指小口啃，所以这个词一直带着一点牙齿的意味，而不只是手指。

normal.en: Pincers is the same family with a tool suffix: the thing that does the pinching for you.
normal.cn: pincers 是同一词族加上表工具的后缀，指的是替你去夹的那样东西。

normal.en: A pinch of salt is not a weight but a gesture, which is why recipes leave the exact amount to the cook.
normal.cn: 一撮盐不是重量而是一个动作，所以菜谱把准确分量留给做饭的人自己拿捏。

normal.en: Pinched cheeks look as if someone had squeezed them thin, so the adjective came to mean drawn and pale.
normal.cn: 憔悴的脸颊像是被人捏得没了肉，于是这个形容词就表示「消瘦苍白」。

normal.en: Feel the pinch turns the finger squeeze into the pressure of a tight budget, and the original image survives intact.
normal.cn: feel the pinch 把手指的挤压变成紧巴巴的预算压力，原先的意象原封不动地保留下来。

abstract.en: A pinch is the smallest grip there is: not a hold, only a reminder that something is held.
abstract.cn: 「一捏」是最小的抓握：不算握住，只提醒你某样东西正被拿在手里。

abstract.en: The same word measures salt, squeezes skin and describes a hard month, because all three are pressure applied to something small.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量盐、又掐皮肤、还形容难熬的一个月，因为三者都是施加在小东西上的压力。

abstract.en: English trusts the hand more than the scale: a cook who says a pinch is measuring with a gesture.
abstract.cn: 英语更信任手而不是秤：说「一撮」的厨师，是用一个动作在量分量。

examples.en: She pinched the bridge of her nose and sighed.
examples.cn: 她捏着鼻梁叹了口气。

examples.en: Add a pinch of pepper to the sauce.
examples.cn: 往酱汁里加一撮胡椒。

examples.en: Like most students, he felt the pinch in the last week of the month.
examples.cn: 和大多数学生一样，他在月底最后一周感到了手头拮据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拼吃」——盘里只剩一点点，两指捏着拼着吃，记住 pinch 既是一撮也是捏。

root: 一般认为源自古法语 pincier（捏、咬、小口啃），更早可追溯到重构的俗拉丁语 pinctiare 与拉丁语 punctum（点、刺）；词源链的中间环节没有直接文献记录。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small, sharp contact of two fingertips; from that gesture come the tiny amount carried in the fingers and the pressure of a budget squeezed too tight.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两指尖短促而尖的一下接触；由这个动作长出指间所夹的一点点分量，以及被夹得过紧的预算压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two fingertips closing on a small fold of skin or on the last grains of salt.
core.cn: 核心意象：拇指与食指合拢，夹住一小片皮肤，或夹住最后几粒盐。

branches.en: a thumb and forefinger closing on the skin of an arm
branches.cn: 拇指与食指在手臂皮肤上合拢

branches.en: a cook shaking the last grains from finger and thumb
branches.cn: 厨师用两指抖下最后几粒盐

branches.en: an empty wallet in the last week of the month
branches.cn: 月底最后一周的空钱包

branches.en: a grip that is felt before it is seen
branches.cn: 先被感觉到、后被告知的一下夹紧

branches.en: a family measuring what is left by the spoonful
branches.cn: 一家人用一勺一勺来量剩下的东西

intro.en: The word is held by an Old French verb, a reconstructed Vulgar Latin form and the Latin noun for a point, plus English endings that build tools and states.
intro.cn: 这个词由古法语动词、重构的俗拉丁语形式、表示「点」的拉丁名词，以及构成工具与状态的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin link is probable rather than proven: the Vulgar Latin verb is reconstructed, and dictionaries present it as the usual explanation.
latinIntro.cn: 它与拉丁语的联系是「很可能」而非「已证明」：俗拉丁语动词属于重构形式，词典通常把它作为通行解释提出。

items.meaning: to squeeze with finger and thumb

items.meaningCN: 表工具或施动者的后缀

definition_zh: 松树；松木；渴望；憔悴
definition_en: a tall evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves, its pale soft wood, or to long for someone so much that you grow thin and dull
core_image: 雪坡上一棵针叶树，细长的针叶托着雪，树皮裂成一片片鳞甲
scene: 冬天的山坡上，一排针叶树顶着雪，树皮裂成一片片鳞甲，风穿过细针一样的叶子发出低低的响声。The old pine at the gate has stood there for a hundred years.
sceneCN: 这里 pine 指「松树」（第 1 个义项：常绿的针叶乔木）；句意为门口那棵老松已经在那里站了一百年。图中可辨识物件：雪坡、针叶、开裂的树皮。

derivatives.zh: 由 pine 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「松树的；松林多的」
由 pine 加表场所的后缀 -ery 构成，义为「松林；松园」
由 pine 加 -ing 构成，义为「苦苦思念；日渐消瘦」

senses.title: An evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves
senses.definition: a tall evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves and woody cones that stays green through the winter
senses.definitionCN: 一种高大的常绿乔木，叶如细针，结木质球果，冬季依然青绿
senses.example: An old pine shades the whole yard.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵老松为整个院子遮阴。
senses.why: Latin pinus was simply the name of this tree, and English borrowed the noun together with the tree, so this is the sense the word started from.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pinus 本来就是这种树的名字，英语连同树一起借来这个名词，所以这是词最原始的义项。

senses.title: The pale soft wood of this tree
senses.definition: the light, soft timber of this tree, used for floors, furniture and paper
senses.definitionCN: 这种树浅色而柔软的木材，用于地板、家具与造纸
senses.example: The floor is made of pine.
senses.exampleCN: 地板是松木做的。
senses.why: Once a tree has a name, its timber takes the same name, because the material is only the tree after it has been cut and sawn.
senses.whyCN: 一种树有了名字，它的木材也就用同一个名字，因为木料不过是砍下锯开之后的树。

senses.title: To long for someone or something
senses.definition: to want someone or something very much, in a way that makes you unhappy
senses.definitionCN: 非常想要某人或某物，想到心里难受
senses.example: She pined for the sea she had left behind.
senses.exampleCN: 她苦苦思念着离开的那片海。
senses.why: The verb came from a different word, an Old English verb for torment; a longing that hurts was pictured as a slow torture, and that ache stayed inside the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 动词另有来源，是古英语中表示「折磨」的动词；令人难受的渴望被想象成一种缓慢的拷问，这份痛感就留在了词义里。

senses.title: To waste away with grief or longing
senses.definition: to become weak, thin and dull because of sorrow, illness or a long wait
senses.definitionCN: 因悲伤、疾病或长久等待而变得虚弱、消瘦、没有神采
senses.example: He pined away after the farm was sold.
senses.exampleCN: 农场卖掉之后，他日渐憔悴。
senses.why: If longing is a torture, the body eventually shows it; pine away names the visible result of that inner strain rather than the feeling itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然渴望是一种折磨，身体迟早会把它显出来；pine away 指的就是这份内在煎熬露在外表上的结果，而不是那股情绪本身。

intro.en: Two different words meet in this spelling: the tree name came from Latin pinus, while the verb for painful longing came from an Old English verb for tormenting.
intro.cn: 这个拼写里其实合流了两个不同的词：树名来自拉丁语 pinus，表示痛苦渴望的动词则来自古英语中表示折磨的动词。

items.en: Latin pinus named the pine tree and could also mean its wood or resin; the same name travelled around the Mediterranean.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pinus 是松树的名字，也可指松木或松脂；同一个名称在地中海各地通行。

items.en: Old English borrowed the tree name as pin, and the modern spelling later added a final e to match the verb.
items.cn: 古英语把树名借入写作 pin，现代拼写后来加了一个词尾 e，好与动词的写法统一。

items.en: A separate Old English verb pinian meant to torture or torment; it came from pin, a noun for pain that is generally traced back to Latin poena.
items.cn: 另有一个古英语动词 pinian，意为折磨、拷问；它来自表示痛苦的名词 pin，而这个词一般认为可追溯到拉丁语 poena。

items.en: Middle English kept both words, so pinen could mean to suffer and also to yearn painfully for something lost.
items.cn: 中古英语把两个词都保留下来，于是 pinen 既指受苦，也指为失去的东西痛苦地思念。

items.en: Modern English holds the tree, its timber, the ache of longing and the visible wasting away, with the two histories now written as one word.
items.cn: 现代英语同时容纳了树、木材、思念之苦与看得见的消瘦，两段来历如今写成同一个词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the tree's own family and a few words that only look similar; the near-meaning group pairs other conifers with other verbs of longing.
note.cn: 形近组收这棵树自己的词族，以及几个只是看起来相似的词；近义组把其他针叶树与别的「渴望」动词配在一起。

normalIntro.en: A tree name and a verb of torment happen to share one spelling, and the whole family divides neatly between wood and longing.
normalIntro.cn: 一个树名和一个表示折磨的动词恰好共用一个拼写，整个词族也就清楚地分成「木」与「渴望」两半。

normal.en: Latin pinus is the tree, which is why botany still uses pinus for the genus and why pine needles resist frost.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pinus 就是这种树，所以植物学至今用 pinus 作属名，松针也才那么耐霜。

normal.en: The verb pine never grew out of the tree; it came from an Old English word for torment, so pine for and pine tree are only spelling twins.
normal.cn: 动词 pine 并不是从树长出来的，它来自古英语中表示折磨的词，所以 pine for 与 pine tree 只是拼写上的双胞胎。

normal.en: Pine away adds away to the verb: the person is not only longing but visibly losing weight and colour.
normal.cn: pine away 在动词后加 away：人不只是思念，还肉眼可见地掉肉、褪色。

normal.en: Pinery uses -ery, the same place suffix as in bakery and brewery, so it means a place of pines.
normal.cn: pinery 用 -ery，与 bakery、brewery 里那个表场所的后缀相同，所以意思是「松树之地」。

normal.en: Pineal keeps the cone image: the gland was named for its shape, not for any connection with timber.
normal.cn: pineal 保留了松果的形象：那个腺体是因形状得名，与木材没有关系。

abstract.en: A pine keeps its needles all winter, and English keeps two unrelated words under one spelling just as stubbornly.
abstract.cn: 松树整个冬天都不落叶，英语也同样固执地把两个不相干的词留在一个拼写下。

abstract.en: The same four letters can mean shade, floorboards, heartache and weight loss, which is a reminder that context does the sorting.
abstract.cn: 同样四个字母可以指树荫、地板、心痛与消瘦，这提醒人：分辨词义的是上下文。

abstract.en: To pine is to be pulled toward something absent; the tree simply stands where it is, which is why the two images never mix.
abstract.cn: pine 是被拉向缺席之物；而松树只是站在原地，所以这两个意象从不混淆。

examples.cn: 一棵老松为整个院子遮阴。

examples.en: She pined for the sea she had left behind.
examples.cn: 她苦苦思念着离开的那片海。

senses.title: A British unit of liquid volume
senses.definition: a unit of liquid volume used in Britain, equal to about 568 millilitres, or one eighth of an imperial gallon
senses.definitionCN: 英国使用的液量单位，约合五百六十八毫升，即一英制加仑的八分之一
senses.example: A pint of milk is still the standard bottle here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，一品脱装的牛奶仍是标准瓶装。
senses.why: The measure came through Old French, where a pinte was the marked measure on a drinking vessel, so the unit began as a mark on a container rather than as an abstract number.
senses.whyCN: 这个量经古法语传来，那里的 pinte 指饮酒器上刻出的那道量记，所以这个单位最初是容器上的一道刻痕，而不是一个抽象数字。

senses.title: The smaller American unit of the same name
senses.definition: a unit of liquid volume used in the United States, equal to about 473 millilitres, or one eighth of a US gallon
senses.definitionCN: 美国使用的液量单位，约合四百七十三毫升，即一美制加仑的八分之一
senses.example: The recipe asks for a pint of cream.
senses.exampleCN: 这份食谱需要一品脱奶油。
senses.why: Britain and America kept the same word but fixed different gallons, so one name ended up measuring two different amounts, and only the context tells them apart.
senses.whyCN: 英美保留了同一个词，却把「加仑」定成不同的量，于是一个名字最后量出两种分量，只能靠上下文分辨。

senses.title: A glass of beer ordered by that measure
senses.definition: a glass of beer, especially in a pub, sold in this measure and treated as a single drink
senses.definitionCN: 按这个分量售出的一杯啤酒，尤指酒馆里当作一份饮品来卖
senses.example: He ordered a pint and sat by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他要了一品脱啤酒，坐到窗边。
senses.why: In a pub the measure becomes the order itself, so people stopped saying a pint of beer and simply asked for a pint, and the container now stands for the drink.
senses.whyCN: 在酒馆里，那个分量本身成了点单的单位，于是人们不再说「一品脱啤酒」，干脆只说「来一品脱」，容器就这样代替了饮料。

intro.en: Pint goes back through French to a Latin idea of a painted mark, because the first measures were marks cut or painted on the side of a jar.
intro.cn: pint 经法语上溯到拉丁语中「画上的记号」这一观念，因为最早的量具就是刻在或画在罐子侧壁上的记号。

items.en: Latin pingere meant to paint or to mark, and its participle picta described something that had been painted.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pingere 意为画、作记号，其分词 picta 指「被画过的」。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin pincta is generally assumed to mean a painted mark, the sort of line that showed how much a jar held.
items.cn: 一般认为俗拉丁语 pincta 意为「画上的记号」，即标示罐子容量的那种刻线。

items.en: Old French pinte named both a liquid measure and the marked vessel that carried the mark, and it passed into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 pinte 既指一种液量，也指带着那道记号的量器，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English used pinte for ale, wine and milk, and the spelling slowly settled into the modern pint.
items.cn: 中古英语用 pinte 量麦酒、葡萄酒与牛奶，拼写慢慢固定为现代的 pint。

items.en: Modern English kept a British pint of about 568 millilitres and an American pint of about 473 millilitres, and the pub turned the measure into a drink you can order.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了约五百六十八毫升的英制品脱与约四百七十三毫升的美制品脱，酒馆又把这个分量变成可以直接点的一杯酒。

normal.cn: 拉丁语 pingere 意为画，所以品脱最初是罐子上画的一道线，而不是书上的一个数字。

normal.en: Old French pinte named the vessel as well as the amount, which is why English can say a pint glass and a pint of milk with the same word.
normal.cn: 古法语 pinte 既指容器也指分量，所以英语能用同一个词说「品脱杯」和「一品脱牛奶」。

normal.en: The British and American pints differ because each country fixed its own gallon, and the word never split to show it.
normal.cn: 英制品脱与美制品脱不同，是因为两国各自定了加仑，而这个词并没有分裂成两个写法来提示差别。

normal.en: Half a pint is the usual small measure in a pub, and half-pint is also a joking name for a short person.
normal.cn: 半品脱是酒馆里常见的小份，half-pint 也被拿来戏称个子矮小的人。

normal.en: Pint-sized keeps the container image: a person described that way looks as if they were poured into a very small glass.
normal.cn: pint-sized 保留了容器的意象：被这样形容的人，像是被倒进了一只很小的杯子。

abstract.en: A unit named after a mark reminds us that measuring began with scratches on pottery, not with mathematics.
abstract.cn: 以一道记号命名的单位提醒人：测量始于陶器上的刻痕，而不是数学。

abstract.en: One word, two countries, two amounts: a pint is a good example of how a shared language can disagree with itself.
abstract.cn: 同一个词、两个国家、两种分量：品脱正好说明，同一种语言也会跟自己不一致。

abstract.en: When the measure becomes the order, the glass is doing the talking, and nobody needs to name the liquid.
abstract.cn: 当分量变成点单的说法，杯子就在替人说话，谁也不必再点明杯里是什么。

examples.en: A pint of milk is still the standard bottle here.
examples.cn: 在这里，一品脱装的牛奶仍是标准瓶装。

examples.en: He ordered a pint and sat by the window.
examples.cn: 他要了一品脱啤酒，坐到窗边。

examples.en: The recipe asks for a pint of cream.
examples.cn: 这份食谱需要一品脱奶油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派恩特」——派对上把杯子一摁，正好量出一品脱；记住 pint 是容量单位。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 pingere（画、作记号）的分词 picta，经俗拉丁语 pincta（画上的刻记）与古法语 pinte 进入英语；中间的俗拉丁语形式属于重构，未见文献记录。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a marked measure on a vessel; the same mark becomes a British unit, an American unit and finally the glass of beer itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是容器上的一道量记；同一道记号先变成英制单位，再变成美制单位，最后变成那一杯啤酒本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick glass with a shallow line cut around it, filled exactly to that line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只厚玻璃杯，杯壁刻着一道浅浅的横线，液体正好注到线。

branches.en: a milk bottle standing on a doorstep
branches.cn: 放在门阶上的牛奶瓶

branches.en: a measuring jug filled to a printed line
branches.cn: 注到印刷刻线的量杯

branches.en: foam settling on the rim of a glass
branches.cn: 泡沫在杯口慢慢沉下

branches.en: two labels saying the same word and meaning different amounts
branches.cn: 两个写着同一个词却分量不同的标签

branches.en: a barman pulling the handle once and setting the glass down
branches.cn: 酒保拉一下手柄，把杯子放下

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of painting, its participle, a reconstructed Vulgar Latin noun and the French and English forms that followed.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示「画」的动词、它的分词、一个重构的俗拉丁语名词，以及随后的法语与英语形式构成。

latinIntro.en: The usual account takes the measure back to a painted mark on a vessel; because the Vulgar Latin noun is reconstructed, the chain is offered as generally accepted rather than certain.
latinIntro.cn: 通行的解释把这一量具追溯到容器上画出的记号；由于俗拉丁语名词是重构形式，这条链只能说是「一般认为」，而非确证。

definition_zh: 管子；管道；烟斗；管乐器；用管道输送；吹奏
definition_en: a hollow tube that carries liquid or gas, a bowl and stem for smoking, a simple wind instrument, or to carry something through such a tube and play such an instrument
core_image: 一根铁管沿墙角转了个弯，管壁上挂着水珠，一头接进墙里，一头通到水池下
scene: 老房子的厨房里，一根铁管沿着墙角转了个弯，一直通到水池下面，管壁上凝着一层细小的水珠。A thin pipe carries hot water up to the radiator.
sceneCN: 这里 pipe 指「管子、管道」（第 1 个义项：输送液体或气体的空心管）；句意为一根细管把热水送上暖气片。图中可辨识物件：铁管、墙角转弯、水珠。

pos.zh: 用管道输送；吹奏；尖声说唱

derivatives.zh: 由 pipe 与 line 复合而成，义为「管道；输油管；输气管」
由 pipe 加表人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「吹笛人；风笛手」
由 pipe 加 -ing 构成，义为「管道系统；尖而高的声音」

senses.title: A hollow tube for carrying liquid or gas
senses.definition: a hollow cylinder, usually of metal or plastic, through which water, gas or oil flows from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 金属或塑料制成的空心圆管，水、煤气或石油在里面从一处流到另一处
senses.example: A burst pipe flooded the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 一根爆裂的水管淹了厨房。
senses.why: The word began as a name for a hollow tube, and water works kept that plain physical sense, which is still the most common one today.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就是空心管子的名字，自来水工程保留了这个最朴素的实物义，它至今仍是最常用的义项。

senses.title: A bowl and stem for smoking tobacco
senses.definition: a small object with a bowl at one end and a hollow stem, used for smoking tobacco
senses.definitionCN: 一端是斗、另一端是空心细杆的小物件，用来吸烟草
senses.example: He filled his pipe and lit it slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 他把烟斗装满，慢慢点上。
senses.why: Tobacco is smoked through a tube with a bowl at the end, so the general name for a tube narrowed onto that one shape, and the object kept the plain word.
senses.whyCN: 烟草要通过一根末端带斗的管子来吸，于是「管子」这个通名就收窄到这一种形状上，物件本身保留了这个朴素的词。

senses.title: A simple wind instrument, or its sound
senses.definition: a simple wind instrument made from a hollow tube with finger holes, or the high sound made by such a tube or by a whistle
senses.definitionCN: 用带指孔的空心管做成的简单吹奏乐器，或这种管子、哨子发出的高音
senses.example: A shepherd played a pipe on the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 牧羊人在山坡上吹着笛子。
senses.why: The earliest pipes were hollow reeds and bones that whistled in the breath, so tube and instrument were one object, and the musical sense is as old as the word.
senses.whyCN: 最早的管是空心的芦苇和骨头，靠气息发声，所以管子和乐器本是同一件东西，音乐义与这个词同样古老。

senses.title: To carry something through a tube
senses.definition: to carry water, gas or another substance from one place to another through pipes
senses.definitionCN: 通过管道把水、煤气或其他物质从一处输送到另一处
senses.example: Fresh water is piped into every house on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 这条街上的每户人家都接通了自来水。
senses.why: Once the noun named the tube, the verb could name what the tube does, so any liquid moved by tubes is piped without any further change of form.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词已指管子，动词自然可以指管子所做的事，于是凡是用管子送走的液体都叫 piped，词形不必再变。

senses.title: To play a pipe or speak in a high voice
senses.definition: to play a pipe, or to speak or sing in a thin, high voice
senses.definitionCN: 吹奏管乐器，或用又细又高的嗓音说话、唱歌
senses.example: She piped a few words that nobody could hear.
senses.exampleCN: 她尖着嗓子说了几句，谁也听不清。
senses.why: The instrument sense produced a verb of playing it, and because the instrument's sound is thin and high, the same verb slid onto voices that sound the same way.
senses.whyCN: 乐器义衍生出「演奏它」的动词，又因为这种乐器的声音又细又高，同一个动词便滑到同样音色的嗓音上。

intro.en: Pipe is a word of imitative origin: the chirping sound came first, then the hollow tube that repeated it, and English borrowed the result from Latin.
intro.cn: pipe 是一个源自拟声的词：先有啾啾的鸣声，再有重复这种声音的空心管，英语从拉丁语借来了最后的结果。

items.en: Latin pipare was an imitative verb for chirping or peeping, and it named the thin sound made by young birds.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pipare 是拟声动词，指啾啾地叫或吱吱地响，专门形容幼鸟发出的细声。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin pipa named a pipe or tube, and it is generally assumed to be formed from the chirping verb, though the step is not directly recorded.
items.cn: 俗拉丁语 pipa 指管子、管道，一般认为它由那个拟声动词构成，不过这一步没有直接文献记录。

items.en: Old English took the word as pipe, meaning a tube and also a whistle or small wind instrument, so the solid and the musical senses arrived together.
items.cn: 古英语把这个词借作 pipe，既指管子，也指哨子或小吹管，于是实物义与音乐义一起进入英语。

items.en: Middle English used pipe for drains and gutters, and from the sixteenth century for the new tobacco pipe, a bowl set on a hollow stem.
items.cn: 中古英语用 pipe 指排水管与檐槽，十六世纪起又用来指新出现的烟斗，即装在空心细杆上的一个斗。

items.en: Modern English adds piped water, pipelines and pipes in computing, and keeps pipe down and pipe up as phrases that still turn on sound.
items.cn: 现代英语添上了自来水、管道运输与计算机里的管道，而 pipe down 与 pipe up 这两个说法仍然绕着声音打转。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the pip- stem and the compounds built on it; the near-meaning group gathers other tubes and other words for a whistling sound.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 pip- 词干以及由它构成的复合词排列；近义组收其他管状物与表示哨音的词。

entries.definition: A person who plays a pipe or a set of pipes.
entries.definitionCN: 吹笛子或吹风笛的人。

entries.definition: A system of pipes, or a thin high sound.
entries.definitionCN: 成套的管道，或又细又高的声音。

entries.definition: A long line of connected pipes carrying oil or gas across country.
entries.definitionCN: 把石油或天然气输送到远方的成串管道。

entries.definition: A thin tube for measuring small amounts of liquid; the French word is a small pipe.
entries.definitionCN: 量取少量液体的细管；这个法语词的本义就是「小管子」。

entries.definition: A long hollow cylinder, especially a soft one.
entries.definitionCN: 细长的空心圆筒，尤指软的管。

entries.definition: A flexible tube used for carrying water.
entries.definitionCN: 用来输水的软管。

entries.definition: A tube or channel built to carry air, heat or cables.
entries.definitionCN: 用来输送空气、热气或电缆的管道。

entries.definition: A small device that makes a high sound when blown, or that sound.
entries.definitionCN: 吹气时发出高音的小装置，或这种声音。

normalIntro.en: A chirping verb, a tube and a whistle share one short word, and every later sense keeps either the hollow shape or the thin sound.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拟声动词、一根管子和一声哨音共用一个短词，后来每个义项都保留着「中空」的形状或「细高」的声音。

normal.en: Latin pipare is a chirping verb, which explains why the same word can mean a tube and a whistle: both are thin and hollow.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pipare 是拟声的「啾啾叫」，这解释了同一个词为何既能指管子又能指哨子：两者都细而中空。

normal.en: The tobacco pipe is only one shape of tube, a bowl fitted to a hollow stem, so English reused the plain word instead of inventing one.
normal.cn: 烟斗只是管子的一种形状，一个斗接在空心细杆上，所以英语直接沿用这个朴素的词，没有再另造新词。

normal.en: Pipeline is pipe plus line, and it names the whole run of joined tubes rather than a single piece.
normal.cn: pipeline 是 pipe 加 line，指的是整条接起来的管线，而不是单独一截。

normal.en: A piper is the person, piping is the act or the whole system, and both keep the -p- sound of the original word.
normal.cn: piper 指人，piping 指动作或整套系统，两者都保留着原词那个短促的 p 音。

normal.en: Pipe down and pipe up come from sound as well: one means lower your voice, the other means start speaking.
normal.cn: pipe down 与 pipe up 也都从声音来：一个叫你压低嗓音，一个叫你开口说话。

abstract.en: A pipe is a promise that something far away can be reached, as long as the tube is not broken.
abstract.cn: 管子是一种承诺：只要它没断，远处的东西就能被接到手边。

abstract.en: The same word carries water, smoke and music, because all three need a hollow space to travel through.
abstract.cn: 同一个词输送水、烟与音乐，因为这三者都需要一段中空的路才能走。

abstract.en: A whistle is a pipe with the water taken out: nothing flows but air, and the sound is the only thing that arrives.
abstract.cn: 哨子就是抽掉了水的管子：没有东西流动，只有空气，最后到达的只有声音。

examples.en: A burst pipe flooded the kitchen.
examples.cn: 一根爆裂的水管淹了厨房。

examples.en: A shepherd played a pipe on the hillside.
examples.cn: 牧羊人在山坡上吹着笛子。

examples.en: Fresh water is piped into every house on the street.
examples.cn: 这条街上的每户人家都接通了自来水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派普」——水从管子里派出去，噗噗地流；记住 pipe 是管子，也是烟斗与笛。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语拟声动词 pipare（啾啾叫），其名词形式经俗拉丁语 pipa（管子）进入古英语 pipe；拟声与「管」之间的中间环节属于推断。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hollow tube; water, smoke, breath and music all pass through it, so the senses divide between what the tube is and what it carries.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一根空心管；水、烟、气息与音乐都从里面经过，所以义项分成「管子是什么」与「管子送什么」两路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metal tube turning a corner along a kitchen wall, beaded with water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根铁管沿厨房墙角转了个弯，管壁上挂着水珠。

branches.en: a burst joint spraying water across a floor
branches.cn: 爆开的接口把水喷了一地

branches.en: a thumb pressing tobacco into a small bowl
branches.cn: 拇指把烟草按进小斗里

branches.en: a reed cut to length with holes burned through
branches.cn: 截成一段、烫出指孔的芦苇

branches.en: water climbing quietly inside a wall
branches.cn: 水在墙里悄悄往上爬

branches.en: a thin note held longer than the breath seems to last
branches.cn: 一个细音拖得比一口气还长

intro.en: A chirping Latin verb, its noun for a tube, the Old English borrowing and the English endings together hold the word and its family.
intro.cn: 一个拟声的拉丁语动词、由它而来的「管」名词、古英语的借入形式，以及英语词尾，共同撑起这个词及其词族。

latinIntro.en: The chirping verb is securely attested; the noun for a tube is usually derived from it, but that step is presented as generally assumed rather than proved.
latinIntro.cn: 拟声动词有可靠记载；表示管子的名词通常被认为由它派生，但这一步只是「一般认为」，并非已经证明。

definition_zh: 坑；深洞；矿井；果核；使凹陷；留下凹坑
definition_en: a deep hole in the ground, a coal mine, the hard stone inside a fruit, or to mark a surface with small hollows
core_image: 雨后的土路上，车轮把软泥压出一个深深的圆坑，里面积着浑水
scene: 雨后的土路上，一辆卡车驶过，车轮把软泥压出一个深深的坑，积水映着天光。The truck's rear wheel dropped into a deep pit beside the road.
sceneCN: 这里是「坑、深洞」（第 1 个义项：地面向下陷出的深洞）；句意为卡车的后轮陷进了路边的深坑。画面里是那个积着浑水的圆坑。

pos.zh: 使凹陷；留下凹坑；把……放进坑里

derivatives.zh: 由 pit 与 fall 复合而成，本指陷阱，引申为「隐患；容易犯的错误」
由 pit 加 -ed 构成，形容表面布满小凹坑的
由 pit 与 stop 复合而成，指赛车中途进站加油换胎，也指长途中的短暂停留

senses.title: A deep hole in the ground
senses.definition: a deep hole in the ground, either natural or dug out by people
senses.definitionCN: 地面上的深洞，或天然形成，或由人挖出
senses.example: Rainwater had collected at the bottom of the pit.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水积在坑底。
senses.why: Old English pytt named a shaft dug down to water or to a grave, so depth and digging are built into the word rather than added later.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pytt 本指向下挖到水层或墓穴的竖井，「往下」和「挖出来」从一开始就写在这个词里，坑的义项并不是后来才借来的比喻。

senses.title: A coal mine or its underground workings
senses.definition: a coal mine, or the shaft and tunnels through which coal is taken from the earth
senses.definitionCN: 煤矿，或从地下取煤的竖井与坑道
senses.example: His grandfather spent forty years down the pit.
senses.exampleCN: 他的祖父在矿井下干了四十年。
senses.why: A mine is only a pit enlarged and followed downward along a seam, so miners kept the plain word for the hole and let it name the whole working.
senses.whyCN: 矿井不过是被放大、并顺着煤层一路往地下延伸的坑；矿工沿用「坑」这个朴素说法，让它指整个开采系统，词义便从「洞」扩成「洞所代表的产业空间」。

senses.title: The hard stone at the centre of a fruit
senses.definition: the hard stone at the centre of a fruit such as a peach or a cherry
senses.definitionCN: 桃、樱桃等果实中心那枚坚硬的核
senses.example: She spat the cherry pit into her hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她把樱桃核吐到手里。
senses.why: A stone sits in a small hollow at the heart of the fruit, and American English took that hollow as the link, transferring the word for a pit to the hard body inside it.
senses.whyCN: 果核正嵌在果实中央一个小凹腔里，美式英语抓住这层「软东西里藏着一个小坑」的相似，把表示坑的词转到了核上，于是「地里的洞」变成了「果肉里的硬核」。

senses.title: To mark or hollow a surface
senses.definition: to make small hollows in a surface, or to become marked with such hollows
senses.definitionCN: 在表面弄出小凹坑，或变得坑坑洼洼
senses.example: Hail had pitted the roof of the old car.
senses.exampleCN: 冰雹把旧车的车顶砸出了一个个小坑。
senses.why: Once the noun names a hollow, the verb only has to name the act of producing one, and English often turns concrete nouns into verbs without adding any suffix.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然已经指一个凹下去的洞，动词就顺理成章指「造出这样的洞」；英语常把这类具体名词直接当动词用，不加词尾，于是「坑」变成了「砸出坑」。

intro.en: Pit is a Germanic word whose oldest recorded English form is pytt, and the word for a well or shaft is generally traced back to Latin puteus.
intro.cn: pit 是一个日耳曼词，英语里最早的形式写作 pytt；表示井、竖井的这个词一般认为可以上溯到拉丁语 puteus。

items.en: Puteus meant a well or a shaft dug down to water, and it is generally taken as the source of the Germanic word for a pit.
items.cn: puteus 意为水井，或向下挖到水层的竖井；一般认为它就是日耳曼语中表示「坑」的那个词的来源。

items.en: A reconstructed West Germanic form is posited as the bridge between puteus and English; it is a reconstruction, not a word found in any text.
items.cn: 学界为 puteus 与英语之间设想了一个西日耳曼语的重构形式作为桥梁；它属于重构，并非任何文本里实际出现的词。

items.en: Old English pytt meant a pit, a well or a grave, and it is recorded early both in place names and in ordinary use.
items.cn: 古英语 pytt 意为坑、井或墓穴，很早便见于地名与日常用语。

items.en: Middle English pit kept the hole and the grave, and the verb pit began to mean putting something into a hole or marking a surface with hollows.
items.cn: 中古英语 pit 保留了「坑」与「墓穴」两义，动词 pit 也开始表示把东西放进坑里，或在表面留下凹坑。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to coal mines, fruit stones and small hollows, and fixes phrases such as pit against and pit stop.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到煤矿、果核与小凹坑，并固定下 pit against 与 pit stop 这类说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built from the word and spellings that merely resemble it; the near-meaning group gathers words for holes, channels and mines.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词构成的形式，以及仅仅外形相似的拼写；近义组收表示洞、沟渠与矿坑的词。

entries.definition: Marked with small hollows, or having had the stone removed, as with olives.
entries.definitionCN: 布满小凹坑的，或已经去核的，如橄榄。

entries.definition: A hidden danger or an easy mistake to make; literally a covered hole to catch animals.
entries.definitionCN: 隐藏的危险或容易犯的错误；字面上是捕捉动物用的暗坑。

entries.definition: The soft spongy tissue inside a stem or under the rind of citrus fruit; it only looks similar and has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 植物茎内或柑橘皮下的海绵状软组织；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sliding part that moves up and down inside a cylinder; the spelling is close but the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 在气缸内上下滑动的部件；拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An opening or hollow in a surface, the plainest word for what a pit is.
entries.definitionCN: 表面上开口或凹陷的地方，是「坑」最朴素的对应词。

entries.definition: A long narrow channel dug in the ground, usually for drainage.
entries.definitionCN: 在地上挖出的狭长沟渠，通常用于排水。

entries.definition: An excavation made to take coal or metal from the earth.
entries.definitionCN: 为开采煤或金属而挖出的矿坑。

entries.definition: A small natural depression in a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 表面上天然形成的小凹陷。

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for a well, its Germanic borrowing, an Old English noun and verb and a set of English compounds hold this word together.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示水井的拉丁词、它在日耳曼语中的借形、古英语的名词与动词，以及一串英语复合词，共同撑起这个词。

normal.en: Puteus in Latin was a well, and the Germanic word for a pit is generally traced to it, so the oldest picture is a shaft dug down for water.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 puteus 是水井，日耳曼语里表示坑的词一般认为来自它，所以最早的画面是一口为了取水而往下挖的竖井。

normal.en: Old English pytt already covered hole, well and grave, which is why the modern word can still sound slightly grim.
normal.cn: 古英语 pytt 已经兼指洞、井与墓穴，所以今天这个词有时仍带着一点阴冷的气息。

normal.en: A coal mine is called the pit because it is simply a much larger hole followed downward along the coal seam.
normal.cn: 煤矿被称为 the pit，因为它不过是一个大得多的洞，顺着煤层一路往下延伸。

normal.en: The fruit sense works by shape: a hard stone sits in a small hollow, so the name of the hollow was transferred to the stone.
normal.cn: 果核义靠形状成立：硬核嵌在一个小凹腔里，于是凹腔的名称被转给了核本身。

normal.en: Pit against comes from setting fighting birds or dogs in a pit, while pit stop comes from the marked area where racing cars are serviced.
normal.cn: pit against 来自把斗鸟或斗犬放进坑里相斗，pit stop 则来自赛车维修所用的划定区域。

abstract.en: A pit is a shape made by absence: we name the hole, not the soil that was taken out of it.
abstract.cn: 坑是由「缺失」构成的一种形状：我们命名的是那个洞，而不是被挖走的土。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps a small enclosed hollow, whether it is a mine, a fruit stone or a pockmark on a roof.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留着一个被围起来的小凹腔，无论它是矿井、果核，还是车顶上的麻点。

abstract.en: The phrase pit against turns a hole in the ground into a place where two forces are made to meet.
abstract.cn: pit against 这个说法把地上的一个洞，变成了让两股力量相遇的地方。

examples.en: The car's rear wheel sank into a deep pit beside the road.
examples.cn: 汽车的后轮陷进了路边一个深坑。

examples.en: He has worked down the pit since he was eighteen.
examples.cn: 他从十八岁起就在矿井下干活。

examples.en: Hail pitted the roof of the old car.
examples.cn: 冰雹把旧车的车顶砸出了一个个小坑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈特」——一铲子劈下去，地上特（别）深的一个坑；pit 就是坑与深洞。

root: 拉丁语 puteus（井、坑）一般被认为是这个日耳曼词的来源，经西日耳曼语进入古英语 pytt（坑、井、墓穴）；同族词多与「向下挖出的空洞」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hollow dug into the ground; from it branch the mine, the fruit stone and the act of marking a surface with small hollows.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一个挖进地里的空洞；矿井、果核以及「在表面砸出小坑」的动作都从它分出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round hollow pressed into wet earth, with muddy water standing at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿泥里压出的一个圆坑，坑底积着一汪浑水。

branches.en: a wheel rut filled with muddy water
branches.cn: 积着泥水的车辙坑

branches.en: a lift cage dropping into the dark
branches.cn: 罐笼沉进黑暗的井下

branches.en: a peach cut open around its stone
branches.cn: 桃子沿核切开

branches.en: hail marking the roof of a car
branches.cn: 冰雹在车顶砸出小坑

branches.en: one hollow seen in soil, in fruit and on metal
branches.cn: 同一个凹腔，出现在土里、果肉里和金属上

intro.en: A Latin noun for a well, its Germanic borrowing, the Old English noun and verb, and a few English compounds hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示水井的拉丁名词、它在日耳曼语中的借形、古英语的名词与动词，以及几个英语复合词，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: The ancestry is recorded through Latin puteus; the West Germanic form that carried it north is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
latinIntro.cn: 这一支的来历可由拉丁语 puteus 追到；把它带向北方的西日耳曼语形式属于重构，而非有文本可查的词。
